• Why drinking less usually makes night-time trips and dehydration worse
• Front-loading: how to move your fluids earlier without cutting the total
• Caffeine and alcohol: the timing rules

• How swollen ankles turn into urine at night, and the afternoon leg-raise

text:
Bone loss doesn't hurt until something breaks. About 1 in 2 women and up to 1 in 4 men over 50 will break a bone because of osteoporosis, and roughly a fifth of older people who break a hip die within a year. Here are 6 common mistakes that quietly weaken bones after 60, from the scan most people skip, to the giant calcium pill, the vitamin D dose that backfired in a trial, the medicines that thin bones, and the fear that keeps people from treatment.

In this video, we go through the published research and the official guidelines, in plain language, so you can have a better conversation with your doctor.

In this video you'll learn:
• Mistake 1: skipping the bone density scan (the 2025 USPSTF recommendation) and why height loss matters
• Mistake 2: one big calcium pill instead of food first (absorption, the upper limit, kidney stones)
• Mistake 3: vitamin D at the extremes (the VITAL trial and the 500,000-unit trial that increased falls)
• Mistake 4: walking but no strength, impact or balance training (the LIFTMOR trial)
• Mistake 5: medicines that quietly thin bones (steroids, long-term heartburn pills, too much thyroid medicine)
• Mistake 6: fear of bone medicines, the real numbers, and why denosumab must never just stop
• Two quick extras: alcohol, smoking and protein

The carrot story began as Second World War propaganda, and bilberry (the blueberry's cousin) failed the most rigorous night-vision studies. But in a 15-year study of more than 2,000 adults over 50, people who ate at least one orange a day had over 60% lower risk of late macular degeneration. Here's what the research really says about fruit, greens, eye vitamins and protecting your sight after 60.

In this video, we go through the published research and the official guidelines, in plain language, so you can have a better conversation with your doctor.

• The four conditions behind most vision loss after 60, and which ones diet may help

For years the rule was simple: the lower your blood sugar, the better. But for many people over 70, the major diabetes guidelines now recommend gentler targets, because low blood sugar can cause falls, confusion, emergency visits and has been linked to dementia.

• The 15-15 rule for treating a low, and when to call for help
